# 2 Kings Chapter 4 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 224v–226r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_004_page_001.jpg, 2KI_004_page_002.jpg, 2KI_004_page_003.jpg, 2KI_004_page_004.jpg

---

**1** The wife of one of the prophets' guild came to Elisha in desperation. "Your servant my husband is dead," she said. "You know he was a man who feared the LORD. But now the creditor is coming to take my two boys as slaves."

**2** Elisha asked her, "What can I do for you? What do you have at home?" She answered, "Nothing at all — except a small jar of olive oil."

**3** "Go and borrow as many empty jars as you can from all your neighbors," he told her. "Don't hold back — get as many as possible.

**4** Then go inside with your sons, shut the door, and start pouring oil into the jars. Set each one aside as it fills."

**5** She left him, shut the door behind herself and her sons, and they began bringing jars to her while she poured.

**6** When every jar was full, she said to her son, "Bring me another." He replied, "There aren't any more." And the oil stopped flowing.

**7** She went and told the man of God. He said, "Go sell the oil, pay off your debt, and you and your sons can live on what's left."

**8** One day Elisha was passing through Shunem, where a prominent woman lived. She insisted he stay for a meal, and from then on, whenever he passed through he would stop there to eat.

**9** She said to her husband, "I'm sure this man who keeps coming through is a holy man of God.

**10** Let's build a small room for him on the roof — with a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp — so he has a place to stay whenever he visits."

**11** One day Elisha came and went up to the room to rest.

**12** He said to his servant Gehazi, "Ask the Shunammite to come here." When she came,

**13** Elisha told Gehazi, "Say to her: 'You've gone to all this trouble for us. What can we do for you? Should we put in a word for you with the king or the army commander?'" She replied, "I have everything I need — I live contentedly among my own people."

**14** Afterward Elisha asked, "What can we do for her?" Gehazi said, "Well, she has no son, and her husband is getting old."

**15** "Call her back," Elisha said. She came and stood in the doorway.

**16** Elisha said, "About this time next year, you will be holding a son in your arms." "No, my lord!" she protested. "Please, man of God — don't raise my hopes like that!"

**17** But the woman did conceive, and the following year she gave birth to a son, just as Elisha had promised.

**18** The boy grew. One day he went out to join his father with the harvest workers.

**19** Suddenly he cried out to his father, "My head! My head!" The father told a servant, "Carry him to his mother."

**20** The servant carried him to his mother, and the boy sat on her lap until noon. Then he died.

**21** She carried him upstairs and laid him on the bed of the man of God. Then she shut the door and left.

**22** She called to her husband, "Send me a servant and a donkey right away — I need to get to the man of God and back."

**23** "Why today?" he asked. "It's not the new moon or the Sabbath." She said simply, "It will be fine."

**24** She saddled the donkey and told the servant, "Go as fast as you can — don't slow down unless I tell you!"

**25** She rode to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When Elisha spotted her in the distance, he said to Gehazi, "Look — it's the Shunammite woman.

**26** Run and meet her. Ask her: 'Are you all right? Is your husband all right? Is the child all right?'" She answered, "Everything is fine."

**27** But when she reached the man of God on the mountain, she grabbed hold of his feet. Gehazi moved to push her away, but Elisha said, "Leave her alone. She is in deep anguish, and the LORD hasn't told me why."

**28** She said, "Did I ask you for a son, my lord? Didn't I say, 'Don't raise my hopes'?"

**29** Elisha said to Gehazi, "Get ready immediately. Take my staff and go. Don't stop to greet anyone on the road, and don't respond if anyone greets you. Lay my staff on the boy's face."

**30** But the boy's mother said, "As surely as the LORD lives and as you live, I am not leaving without you." So Elisha got up and went with her.

**31** Gehazi ran ahead and laid the staff on the boy's face, but there was no sound, no sign of life. He went back to meet Elisha and reported, "The boy hasn't woken up."

**32** When Elisha arrived at the house, the boy was lying dead on the bed.

**33** He went in, closed the door behind them, and prayed to the LORD.

**34** Then he got on the bed and lay on top of the child — mouth to mouth, eyes to eyes, hands to hands. As he stretched himself over the boy, the child's body began to grow warm.

**35** Elisha got up, paced back and forth in the room, then stretched himself over the boy again. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.

**36** Elisha called Gehazi and said, "Tell the Shunammite to come." When she arrived, he said, "Here — pick up your son."

**37** She fell at his feet and bowed to the ground. Then she picked up her son and walked out.

**38** Elisha returned to Gilgal during a famine. While the prophets' guild was meeting with him, he told his servant, "Put the large pot on and make some stew for the group."

**39** One of them went into the field to gather herbs and found a wild vine. He picked a lapful of wild gourds from it and came back and sliced them into the stew pot — not realizing what they were.

**40** When the stew was served, the men started eating, then shouted, "Man of God, there's poison in the pot!" They couldn't eat it.

**41** "Bring me some flour," Elisha said. He threw it into the pot and said, "Serve it now." And there was nothing harmful in it.

**42** A man came from Baal-shalishah, bringing the man of God twenty loaves of barley bread made from the first harvest, along with fresh grain in his sack. Elisha said, "Give it to the people to eat."

**43** His servant protested, "How am I supposed to feed a hundred men with this?" Elisha repeated, "Give it to the people to eat, for this is what the LORD says: 'They will eat and still have leftovers.'"

**44** So he served it, and they ate and had food left over — exactly as the LORD had said.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 1 — Debt slavery:** The widow's crisis exposes the brutal economics underneath Israel's covenant society. Her husband served God faithfully, but his death left his family vulnerable to creditors who could legally take children as bond-slaves. The miracle of the oil is economic liberation.

**Verse 13 — "I live contentedly among my own people":** One of the most quietly powerful lines in the Elisha cycle. She doesn't need political connections. She doesn't want favors from the throne. Her contentment is her strength — which makes the gift of a son all the more loaded, because she didn't ask for something to lose.

**Verse 28 — "Didn't I say, 'Don't raise my hopes'?":** This is the emotional center of the story. She knew better than to want what she couldn't keep. The accusation lands — she warned the prophet, and now the thing she didn't dare hope for has been given and taken away.

**Verses 42-44 — Twenty loaves for a hundred:** The echo with the gospel feeding miracles is unmistakable. Insufficient bread, a prophetic command to distribute anyway, eating with surplus. The pattern is set here, centuries before Galilee.

*— PNEUMA*
